title: Advanced Quoting, Sales Pipeline & Procurement
brief: Eight new sales and procurement capabilities layered on top of the quoting, customer management, and purchase-order engines already in place from BIZ-MS0. Adds an RFQ inbox with PDF/email parse and auto-routing, a weighted-forecast sales pipeline dashboard wired to QuoteAnalyticsEngine and CustomerManagementEngine, a quote follow-up workflow with win/loss reason capture and competitor intelligence, a commission/bonus tracker with tiered rules triggered on invoice payment, a credit management tab with aging alerts and order-hold enforcement, a vendor scorecard with composite quality/delivery metrics, a receiving and inspection page wired to PurchaseOrderEngine and QualityManagementEngine for NCR creation, and a shipping/packing page that generates BOLs and captures tracking numbers on order completion.

phases.title: Sales Pipeline, RFQ Inbox & Quote Follow-Up
phases.description: Build the inbound RFQ intake flow (file upload, auto-parse, assign, status track), the weighted-forecast pipeline dashboard, the quote follow-up reminders with win/loss reason capture, and the commission/bonus tracker. All four units touch quoting and customer data — wire to existing QuoteEstimatorEngine, InstantQuoteEngine, QuoteRevisionEngine, QuoteAnalyticsEngine, and CustomerManagementEngine. Add new dispatcher actions to businessDispatcher as required.

units.title: Add RFQ Inbox Page — receive, parse, assign, track response deadlines

steps.instruction: Read web/src/pages/CustomerPortalPage.tsx (1116 lines) to understand how file upload and customer data flows are currently handled before creating any new code
Read src/tools/dispatchers/businessDispatcher.ts and locate the z.enum action list to understand the current list of business actions and the pattern used for adding new actions
Read src/schemas/businessActionSchemas.ts to understand how schemas are defined — check for any existing rfq_ schemas before creating new ones

In businessDispatcher.ts, add the following four values to the z.enum action list if not already present: 'rfq_create', 'rfq_list', 'rfq_assign', 'rfq_update_status'. Then add case handlers: rfq_create calls quoteEstimatorEngine.createRFQ(args), rfq_list calls quoteEstimatorEngine.listRFQs(args.filters), rfq_assign calls quoteEstimatorEngine.assignRFQ(args.rfq_id, args.assignee_id), rfq_update_status calls quoteEstimatorEngine.updateRFQStatus(args.rfq_id, args.status)

Add Zod schemas to businessActionSchemas.ts for each new action — NO .passthrough() allowed. rfq_create: { customer_id: z.string(), material: z.string().optional(), quantity: z.number().optional(), tolerances: z.string().optional(), deadline: z.string().optional(), process_type: z.enum(['milling','turning','edm','grinding','laser','waterjet','other']).optional(), raw_text: z.string().optional() }. rfq_list: { status: z.enum(['received','reviewing','quoted','won','lost']).optional(), assignee_id: z.string().optional() }. rfq_assign: { rfq_id: z.string(), assignee_id: z.string() }. rfq_update_status: { rfq_id: z.string(), status: z.enum(['received','reviewing','quoted','won','lost']) }

Create web/src/pages/RFQInboxPage.tsx. The page must include: (a) a file upload drop-zone accepting PDF and .eml/.txt files (mime types application/pdf, message/rfc822, text/plain); when a file is dropped, POST the file as multipart/form-data to POST /api/erp/rfq-upload and display parsed fields (material, quantity, tolerances, deadline) in an editable preview form before saving; (b) a table of all RFQs with columns: RFQ ID, customer, material, quantity, process type, received date, response deadline, assignee, status; (c) a countdown timer column showing days/hours remaining until the response deadline — yellow at 48 h, red at 12 h; (d) a status pill with transitions Received → Reviewing → Quoted → Won/Lost; (e) an assign button that opens a dropdown of available estimators and calls rfq_assign
Add the route /app/rfq-inbox to web/src/App.tsx (or the router config file) with lazy import of RFQInboxPage and clearance requirement of 'lead'
Add 'RFQ Inbox' nav item to web/src/components/shell/shellCatalog.ts under the Sales section with path '/app/rfq-inbox', icon 'InboxIcon', and minClearance: 'lead'

Add a POST /api/erp/rfq-upload route to src/routes/erp.ts that accepts multipart/form-data, reads the uploaded file buffer, attempts basic text extraction (PDF: use the existing pdfParse utility if available, otherwise extract raw text; email: read plain text body), then calls quoteEstimatorEngine.parseRFQText(rawText) which must return { material, quantity, tolerances, deadline, process_type } using keyword matching. Store the RFQ record with status 'received' and return the parsed fields plus the rfq_id
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors before proceeding. Verify 0 errors

units.title: Add Sales Pipeline Dashboard — funnel, weighted forecast, conversion, time-in-stage

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts (494 lines) in full to understand the analytics_conversion() and analytics_accuracy() method signatures, their input parameters, and what data they return
Read src/engines/CustomerManagementEngine.ts (276 lines) to understand how customer_pipeline() and customer_analytics() work — look at the return shape and what stage data is included

Create web/src/pages/SalesPipelinePage.tsx with the following sections: (a) Funnel visualization: five vertical columns labeled RFQ | Quoted | Negotiation | Won | Lost. Each column displays the count and total value of quotes in that stage. Compute per-column totals from the live quote list. Use Recharts FunnelChart or a custom CSS funnel built with div widths proportional to quote count. (b) Weighted forecast panel: compute sum(quote_value * probability_pct / 100) across all Quoted and Negotiation stage quotes. Group by expected close month and render a Recharts BarChart with months on x-axis and weighted value on y-axis. (c) Conversion rates table: per customer (top 20 by quote volume) — show total quoted, total won, win rate %, and average margin %. Wire to QuoteAnalyticsEngine.analytics_conversion() via GET /api/erp/quote-analytics-conversion. (d) By process type conversion: same win-rate breakdown but grouped by milling/turning/EDM/grinding/laser/waterjet. (e) Time-in-stage table: for each stage (RFQ/Quoted/Negotiation), show average days and max days a quote has spent in that stage. Compute using (Date.now() - stage_entered_at) for open quotes and (stage_exited_at - stage_entered_at) for closed quotes

Wire data fetching: on mount, call GET /api/erp/customer-pipeline (CustomerManagementEngine.customer_pipeline()) for the full quote list with stage data, and GET /api/erp/quote-analytics-conversion for conversion rates. Use React Query or direct fetch with useState/useEffect — match the pattern already used in CustomersPage.tsx

Add 'Sales Pipeline' to shellCatalog.ts under the Sales section with path '/app/sales-pipeline', icon 'TrendingUpIcon', minClearance: 'lead'
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

units.title: Add Quote Follow-Up Workflow — auto-reminders, win/loss reasons, competitor intel

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts (494 lines) to find how analytics_update_outcome() stores quote outcomes. Identify whether win_loss_reason and competitor data fields exist on the outcome record before adding new methods

Add two new methods to QuoteAnalyticsEngine.ts: analytics_win_loss_reason(params: { quote_id: string; outcome: 'won' | 'lost'; reason: WinLossReason; notes?: string }) and analytics_competitor_intel(params: { quote_id: string; competitor_name: string; competitor_price?: number; won_by_competitor: boolean }). Define the WinLossReason type as: 'price' | 'lead_time' | 'capability' | 'relationship' | 'quality' | 'other'. Both methods update the analytics record for the quote_id and call persist()

Add 'analytics_win_loss_reason' and 'analytics_competitor_intel' to the z.enum action list in businessDispatcher.ts. Add case handlers calling quoteAnalyticsEngine.analytics_win_loss_reason(args) and quoteAnalyticsEngine.analytics_competitor_intel(args)

Implement auto-reminder scheduling: in QuoteRevisionEngine.ts, when quote_status_change() transitions a quote to status 'sent', schedule follow-up reminders at 3, 7, and 14 days. Use a lightweight in-process scheduler — store reminder records in a new reminders Map<string, ReminderRecord[]> within QuoteRevisionEngine where ReminderRecord has { quote_id, due_at: Date, day_mark: 3|7|14, sent: boolean }. Add a checkReminders() method that scans the map for unsent reminders where due_at <= now and calls NotificationEngine.notify() for each. Wire checkReminders() to a setInterval(checkReminders, 60_000) started in the constructor, cleared in a destroy() method

Add a follow-up queue section to web/src/pages/QuoteAnalyticsPage.tsx (or QuoteBuilderPage.tsx — read both file headers to determine which already imports QuoteAnalyticsEngine and has a follow-up concept). The section shows: a table of open quotes with columns Quote ID, Customer, Value, Days Since Sent, Next Reminder, Win/Loss (for closed quotes). For won/lost quotes, add an inline form with a reason dropdown (price/lead_time/capability/relationship/quality/other), an optional notes textarea, and optional competitor name + price fields. On submit, call analytics_win_loss_reason and optionally analytics_competitor_intel
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

units.title: Add Commission/Bonus Tracker — tiered rules, per-salesperson earned/pending/paid, invoice trigger

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/InvoicingEngine.ts to identify the invoice_payment() method signature (or equivalent payment event trigger). Determine whether it already emits an event or calls a callback that could hook commission calculation. Read the full file before planning changes

Create src/engines/CommissionEngine.ts. Export a singleton commissionEngine. The engine must contain: (a) CommissionRule interface: { id: string; salesperson_id: string; tier_brackets: Array<{ threshold_dollars: number; rate_pct: number }>; quarterly_target: number; team_bonus_pool_pct: number; effective_from: string }. Default tier: 0–10K at 5%, 10K–50K at 7%, 50K+ at 10%. (b) CommissionRecord interface: { id: string; salesperson_id: string; invoice_id: string; invoice_amount: number; margin_amount: number; commission_amount: number; status: 'earned' | 'pending' | 'paid'; earned_at: string; paid_at?: string }. (c) Methods: configureRule(salesperson_id, rule), calculateCommission(salesperson_id, invoice_id, margin_amount): CommissionRecord — applies tiered brackets to margin_amount, stores and returns record with status='earned'; payout(record_ids: string[]): void — marks records as paid with paid_at timestamp; getSummary(salesperson_id): { earned: number; pending: number; paid: number; ytd_total: number }. (d) Register commissions and commission_rules Maps with persistenceBridge in the constructor. Call persist() after every mutation

In InvoicingEngine.ts, after recording a successful payment in the invoice_payment() handler (or equivalent), call commissionEngine.calculateCommission(invoice.salesperson_id, invoice_id, invoice.margin_amount) if invoice.salesperson_id is defined. Import commissionEngine lazily to avoid circular dependencies

Add three new actions to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'commission_configure', 'commission_calculate', 'commission_payout'. Case handlers: commission_configure calls commissionEngine.configureRule(args.salesperson_id, args.rule); commission_calculate calls commissionEngine.calculateCommission(args.salesperson_id, args.invoice_id, args.margin_amount); commission_payout calls commissionEngine.payout(args.record_ids)

Wire to GET /api/erp/commission-summary?salesperson_id. (b) Commission records table — columns: date, invoice ID, invoice amount, margin, commission amount, status pill (earned/pending/paid), payout button for earned records. (c) Rules configuration panel (visible to hr_manager+): shows current tier brackets as an editable table of threshold/rate pairs, quarterly target input, save button calling commission_configure

phases.title: Credit Management, Vendor Scorecard, Receiving & Shipping
phases.description: Four procurement and fulfillment capabilities: customer credit limits and aging hold enforcement wired into CustomerManagementEngine and InvoicingEngine; a vendor scorecard engine and page with composite quality/delivery metrics from PurchaseOrderEngine; a receiving and inspection page wired to po_receive and NCR creation; and a shipping/packing page with BOL generation and tracking number capture wired to OrderManagerEngine. Three new engine files (CommissionEngine already created in P1), plus new dispatcher actions and pages.

units.title: Add Customer Credit Management — credit limits, payment terms, aging alerts, order-hold enforcement

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/CustomerManagementEngine.ts (276 lines) in full to understand the customer data model — identify whether credit_limit, payment_terms, and credit_status fields already exist on the Customer interface before adding anything

If missing, add the following to the Customer interface in CustomerManagementEngine.ts: credit_limit: number (default 0 = unlimited); payment_terms: 'Net30' | 'Net45' | 'Net60' | 'COD' | 'Prepay' (default 'Net30'); credit_status: 'good' | 'warning' | 'hold' (default 'good'); credit_hold_since?: string (ISO date, set when status transitions to 'hold')

Add a computeCreditStatus(customer_id: string): { status: 'good' | 'warning' | 'hold'; overdue_30: number; overdue_60: number; oldest_overdue_days: number } method to CustomerManagementEngine.ts. It calls InvoicingEngine.getAgingReport(customer_id) (or equivalent aging method — read InvoicingEngine.ts first to find the exact method). Returns 'good' if oldest_overdue_days < 30, 'warning' if 30–60, 'hold' if > 60. Update customer.credit_status accordingly and persist()

Add a checkCreditHold(customer_id: string): { blocked: boolean; reason: string } method to CustomerManagementEngine.ts. Returns { blocked: true, reason: 'Credit hold: invoice overdue >60 days' } when credit_status === 'hold'. This method must be called from OrderManagerEngine.createOrder() before accepting any new order for the customer

Read src/engines/OrderManagerEngine.ts and add a credit hold check at the start of createOrder(): call customerManagementEngine.checkCreditHold(customer_id). If blocked is true, throw an Error with the reason string and HTTP status 403. Import customerManagementEngine lazily to avoid circular dependencies

In web/src/pages/CustomersPage.tsx (531 lines), add a 'Credit' tab to the customer detail view. The tab must show: credit_limit field (editable input, number, updates via customer_update action), payment_terms selector (Net30/Net45/Net60/COD/Prepay), credit_status pill (green=good, yellow=warning, red=hold), aging summary cards (current, 1–30 days overdue, 31–60 days, 60+ days), and a 'Refresh Credit Status' button that calls computeCreditStatus. If status is 'hold', display a red banner: 'Orders blocked — invoice overdue >60 days'
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

deliverables.description: Customer interface with credit_limit, payment_terms, credit_status, credit_hold_since; computeCreditStatus() and checkCreditHold() methods

exit_conditions: Customer interface has credit_limit, payment_terms, credit_status, credit_hold_since

units.title: Add Vendor Scorecard — composite quality/delivery score, trend charts, PO-sourced data

steps.instruction: Check ENGINE_DIGEST.md for any existing vendor scorecard or vendor performance engine before creating a new one. If one exists, read it and wire to it instead of creating VendorScorecardEngine.ts

Read src/engines/PurchaseOrderEngine.ts (315 lines) in full to understand how PO receipt data is stored — specifically what fields are available for delivery date, expected date, line item quality rejection, and vendor_id

Create src/engines/VendorScorecardEngine.ts (only if no equivalent exists). Export a singleton vendorScorecardEngine. Define VendorScore interface: { vendor_id: string; vendor_name: string; on_time_delivery_pct: number; quality_rejection_rate_pct: number; price_competitiveness_score: number; lead_time_reliability_score: number; composite_score: number; month_scores: Array<{ month: string; composite: number }> }. Define composite_score = (on_time_delivery_pct * 0.40) + ((100 - quality_rejection_rate_pct) * 0.35) + (price_competitiveness_score * 0.15) + (lead_time_reliability_score * 0.10)

Implement vendor_score_calculate(vendor_id: string): VendorScore in VendorScorecardEngine.ts. Fetch all completed POs for the vendor from purchaseOrderEngine.listPOsByVendor(vendor_id) (or equivalent). Compute: on_time_delivery_pct = (POs where received_date <= expected_date) / total_POs * 100; quality_rejection_rate_pct = (total rejected line items) / (total received line items) * 100; lead_time_reliability_score = 100 - clamp((stddev of actual_lead_time - quoted_lead_time) * 5, 0, 100); price_competitiveness_score = 100 (placeholder until multi-vendor comparison is available — add TODO). Compute month_scores for trailing 12 months by filtering POs by received_date month

Implement vendor_score_list(): VendorScore[] returning all scored vendors sorted by composite_score descending. Implement vendor_score_trend(vendor_id: string, months: number = 12): Array<{ month: string; composite: number }> returning the month_scores array for the vendor. Register a vendor_scores Map with persistenceBridge in constructor, call persist() after vendor_score_calculate()

Add three actions to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'vendor_score_calculate', 'vendor_score_list', 'vendor_score_trend'. Add case handlers calling vendorScorecardEngine.vendor_score_calculate(args.vendor_id), vendorScorecardEngine.vendor_score_list(), and vendorScorecardEngine.vendor_score_trend(args.vendor_id, args.months)

Add Zod schemas to businessActionSchemas.ts — NO .passthrough(). vendor_score_calculate: { vendor_id: z.string() }. vendor_score_list: { sort_by: z.enum(['composite','delivery','quality','price','lead_time']).optional() }. vendor_score_trend: { vendor_id: z.string(), months: z.number().int().min(1).max(24).optional() }

Add VendorScorecardEngine to BusinessStore.ts ENTITY_CONFIGS: vendor_scores entity with knownColumns [vendor_id, vendor_name, on_time_delivery_pct, quality_rejection_rate_pct, price_competitiveness_score, lead_time_reliability_score, composite_score] and jsonColumns [month_scores]

Create web/src/pages/VendorScorecardPage.tsx with: (a) ranked vendor table — columns: rank, vendor name, on-time delivery %, quality rejection rate %, price score, lead time score, composite score (bold), trend arrow (up/down vs last month); (b) clicking a vendor row expands a 12-month Recharts LineChart of composite_score over time; (c) a 'Recalculate' button per vendor row that calls vendor_score_calculate

Add route /app/vendor-scorecard with lazy import of VendorScorecardPage and clearance 'lead'. Add to shellCatalog.ts under the Procurement section with path '/app/vendor-scorecard', icon 'StarIcon', minClearance: 'lead'
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors

units.title: Add Receiving & Inspection Page — receive against PO, incoming inspection, NCR on reject, lot tracking

steps.instruction: Read src/engines/PurchaseOrderEngine.ts (315 lines) in full. Identify the po_receive() method signature — check what parameters it accepts and what it returns. Also check whether lot_number is stored anywhere on receipt records
Read src/engines/QualityManagementEngine.ts to find the ncr_create() method signature — check required parameters (part number, vendor, defect description, quantity, severity)

If po_receive() does not already accept lot_number, enhance it to accept { po_id: string; line_items: Array<{ po_line_id: string; quantity_received: number; lot_number: string; inspection_result: 'accept' | 'reject' | 'conditional' }> } as its params. Update the PoReceipt record to store lot_number per line. If it already accepts these fields, skip this step

units.title: Add Shipping & Packing Page — packing list, BOL, carrier selection, tracking number capture

steps.instruction: Check ENGINE_DIGEST.md for any existing shipping or logistics engine before creating ShippingEngine.ts

Read src/engines/OrderManagerEngine.ts to understand how order completion is represented — identify the method that marks an order as complete/shipped and what fields are available (customer_id, line_items, part_number, quantity, job_id)

Create src/engines/ShippingEngine.ts. Export a singleton shippingEngine. Define interfaces: PackingList { id: string; order_id: string; customer_id: string; created_at: string; lines: Array<{ part_number: string; description: string; quantity: number; lot_number?: string; job_id?: string }>; status: 'draft' | 'confirmed' | 'shipped' }. BillOfLading { id: string; packing_list_id: string; carrier: Carrier; service_level: string; weight_lbs: number; dimensions?: string; tracking_number?: string; bol_number: string; created_at: string }. Carrier: 'UPS' | 'FedEx' | 'LTL_Freight' | 'Customer_Pickup' | 'Other'. Implement: ship_packing_list(order_id: string): PackingList — fetches order lines from OrderManagerEngine and creates a PackingList in 'draft' status; ship_bol(packing_list_id: string, params: { carrier: Carrier; service_level: string; weight_lbs: number; dimensions?: string }): BillOfLading — generates a BOL with auto-incremented bol_number (format: BOL-YYYYMMDD-NNNN); ship_carrier_select(bol_id: string, carrier: Carrier, service_level: string): void — updates carrier on an existing BOL; ship_tracking(bol_id: string, tracking_number: string): void — records tracking number, marks PackingList as 'shipped', and calls orderManagerEngine.completeOrder(order_id) to mark the order complete. Register packing_lists and bills_of_lading Maps with persistenceBridge. Call persist() after every mutation

Add four actions to businessDispatcher.ts z.enum: 'ship_packing_list', 'ship_bol', 'ship_carrier_select', 'ship_tracking'. Add case handlers: ship_packing_list calls shippingEngine.ship_packing_list(args.order_id); ship_bol calls shippingEngine.ship_bol(args.packing_list_id, args); ship_carrier_select calls shippingEngine.ship_carrier_select(args.bol_id, args.carrier, args.service_level); ship_tracking calls shippingEngine.ship_tracking(args.bol_id, args.tracking_number)

Add Zod schemas to businessActionSchemas.ts — NO .passthrough(). ship_packing_list: { order_id: z.string() }. ship_bol: { packing_list_id: z.string(), carrier: z.enum(['UPS','FedEx','LTL_Freight','Customer_Pickup','Other']), service_level: z.string(), weight_lbs: z.number().positive(), dimensions: z.string().optional() }. ship_carrier_select: { bol_id: z.string(), carrier: z.enum(['UPS','FedEx','LTL_Freight','Customer_Pickup','Other']), service_level: z.string() }. ship_tracking: { bol_id: z.string(), tracking_number: z.string().min(1) }

Add ShippingEngine to BusinessStore.ts ENTITY_CONFIGS: packing_lists entity with knownColumns [id, order_id, customer_id, created_at, status] and jsonColumns [lines]; bills_of_lading entity with knownColumns [id, packing_list_id, carrier, service_level, weight_lbs, dimensions, tracking_number, bol_number, created_at] and jsonColumns []

Create web/src/pages/ShippingPage.tsx with a three-step wizard flow: Step 1 — Order selection: a text input to enter order_id (or scan barcode), a 'Generate Packing List' button that calls ship_packing_list and displays the generated packing list table (part number, description, quantity, lot number, job ID). Step 2 — BOL creation: form fields for carrier dropdown (UPS/FedEx/LTL Freight/Customer Pickup/Other), service level text input (e.g. 'Ground', '2-Day Air'), weight in lbs number input, optional dimensions text input. A 'Create BOL' button calls ship_bol and displays the generated BOL number. Step 3 — Tracking: a text input for tracking number, a 'Mark Shipped' button that calls ship_tracking. On success display a green confirmation card with BOL number, carrier, tracking number, and ship date. Also display a printable packing list (use @media print CSS to format for letter paper)
Add route /app/shipping to the router config with lazy import of ShippingPage and clearance 'shop_floor'
Add 'Shipping' to shellCatalog.ts under the Fulfillment section (create section if absent) with path '/app/shipping', icon 'TruckIcon', minClearance: 'shop_floor'
Run npm run build:fast and verify 0 errors
